doc.title: Lionel Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Buying jazz arrangements from Joey (George) Williams
summary: Hampton bought about fifty arrangements at $10 each, funded by Joe Glaser's advance, and spent the rest on a mink coat for his wife.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, he played lead. And I got Lee Young, who was Lester Young’s brother, playing drums with me. And I kept picking up men like that until I picked up a 16 piece band. And so I got some arrangements from a guy by the name of Joey Williams, who had a book of arrangements, and I got, and he was a terrific arranger. The first arrangement that, oh, what’s the big band leader’s name? What I’m going to tell you, you’re going to be shocked. Glenn Miller. This guy arranged for Glenn Miller. Because it wasn’t Glenn Miller’s idea, it was this guy’s idea, his name was Joey Williams.
For the way the reed section worked?

Yeah. It was Joey Williams. But George Williams, see I didn’t pick out the classic arrangements that he had arranged for Glenn Miller, I picked out the jazz arrangements. So George Williams, I got those arrangements from Williams, and the funny thing about it, we got these arrangements at $10 a piece. At $10 a piece. Because Joe Glaser, a big booker, well he wanted to secure my band, and I put a price and I said you can have it if you give me ten thousand dollars in advance. Well the arrangements were so cheap, that I got about 50 arrangements and oh, I got a whole lot of them for that. And I took the rest of the money and bought my wife a mink coat.
Good deal. I’ll bet she liked that deal too.
